title: Check yourself: what a field holds

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A host's 0110 is unpacked, and its field 55 is an ISOBinaryField holding 12 bytes. Your code calls response.getString(55). What does it return?

options.text: A 24-character string, since getString writes each byte as two hex digits
options.says: getString on a binary field returns the hex form of its bytes

options.text: A 12-character string, since getString maps each byte to the character with that code
options.says: that is what getBytes does in reverse for text; getString on bytes gives hex

options.text: No string at all but null, since getString has no text to give for a byte field
options.says: getString returns null for an absent field or a nested message, not for bytes

options.text: No string at all but an exception, since a byte field must be read with getBytes
options.says: getString never throws for a field it can't read as text; on bytes it gives hex

origin.section: 6.1 A Field Holds Text, Bytes or a Message

questions.stem: A gateway gets an 8-byte PIN block from a web form as 16 hex characters. It calls request.set(52, pinHex) on a new ISOMsg and hands the message to the MUX. The channel's packager declares field 52 as binary. What happens?

options.text: The field holds 16 characters, so packing on the channel fails and the request never leaves
options.says: with no packager attached at set time the value stays text, and the binary field packager refuses 16 for 8

options.text: The field holds 16 characters, so the host receives 32 hex digits and rejects the PIN
options.says: the binary packager refuses the 16-character value; nothing is sent

options.text: The field holds 8 bytes, since set asks the packager the message will travel with
options.says: set uses only a packager already attached to the message; the channel attaches its own at send time

options.text: The field holds 8 bytes, since set sees hex digits and stores the bytes they spell
options.says: set(n, String) converts only when an attached packager says the field is binary

origin.section: 6.2 Binary Data Goes In as Bytes

questions.stem: Your client's channel uses the stock iso87ascii.xml. The host puts a loyalty tier in sub-field 3 of field 62 of its responses. What does response.getString("62.3") return for a response that carries it?

options.text: The tier, since jPOS splits a received field into sub-fields when a path asks
options.says: only the packager splits a field, and the stock one declares 62 as plain text

options.text: The tier, since the host's message carries its sub-field layout with the data
options.says: the layout lives in the packager on each side, never in the message

options.text: null, since field 62 arrives as plain text with no nested message inside it
options.says: unpacked without a declaration the field is text, and every dotted path into it returns null without an error

options.text: null, since a dotted path finds sub-fields your own code put into the message
options.says: a dotted path reads any nested message, including one a declaring packager unpacked

origin.section: 6.3.1 The Receiving Side Needs the Declaration Too

questions.stem: One step of a client sets 48.1 and 48.2 with dotted paths. A later step does ISOMsg f = new ISOMsg(48); f.set(3, "Y"); request.set(f). Which sub-fields does field 48 hold afterwards?

options.text: Only 3, since set puts the new component in place of the one under that number
options.says: set(ISOComponent) replaces whatever the field held; dotted paths add to a nested message

options.text: Only 1 and 2, since set ignores a component whose field number is already in use
options.says: set replaces an existing field; it never ignores the new component

options.text: 1, 2 and 3, since set merges a nested message into the one already there
options.says: set does not merge; the earlier nested message is dropped

options.text: 1, 2 and 3, since sub-fields are stored under their full path such as 48.3
options.says: sub-fields live inside the nested ISOMsg(48), which the new component replaced

origin.section: 6.3 Sub-fields Are a Nested Message That Only a Declaring Packager Can Carry

questions.stem: A gateway keeps each purchase it receives and forwards a copy made with clone(). Once the copy is sent, it calls Arrays.fill(copy.getBytes(52), (byte) 0) to clear the PIN block from memory. What does the kept purchase's field 52 hold now?

options.text: Zeros, since the copy and the original share the array that holds the PIN block
options.says: clone shares leaf components, and getBytes returns the array itself

options.text: Zeros, since clone() links the two messages and a change to the copy reaches the original
options.says: set and unset on the copy leave the original alone; only writes into a shared array reach it

options.text: The PIN block, since clone() gives the copy its own array for each byte field
options.says: clone gives the copy its own field map and nested messages, but byte fields are shared

options.text: The PIN block, since getBytes returns a fresh copy of the bytes on each call
options.says: getBytes returns the stored array, so writing into it changes the field

origin.section: 6.4 A Follow-up Copies the Fields It Lists and Leaves the Original Alone

concepts: A field holds text, bytes or a nested message, and getString gives hex for bytes and null for a nested message.
A clone shares its text and byte components with the original, so a write into a copied array changes both.
A receiver whose packager does not declare the sub-fields gets the field as text and null for every sub-field, without an error.
